materials.title: Variance Assumptions in Regression
materials.body:
## Variance and Error Terms

In regression analysis, the error term captures influences on the dependent variable that are not explained by the model.

### Homoscedasticity

The variance of errors remains roughly constant across all observations.

### Heteroscedasticity

The variance of errors changes across observations. Error spread may increase or decrease as values of an explanatory variable change.

Economists care about heteroscedasticity because it can make standard errors unreliable and affect statistical inference.

materials.title: Comparing Constant and Changing Variance
materials.body:
## Worked Example

Model A:

1. Residuals remain similarly spread at low and high values.
2. Variance appears stable.
3. Conclusion: homoscedasticity.

Model B:

1. Residuals are tightly grouped at low values.
2. Residual spread widens as values increase.
3. Variance changes across observations.
4. Conclusion: heteroscedasticity.

materials.title: Example Conceptual Explanation
materials.body: Homoscedasticity occurs when error variance remains constant across observations. Heteroscedasticity occurs when error variance changes. The difference matters because changing variance can distort standard errors and make statistical tests less reliable.

materials.title: Concept Check
materials.body:
- Defined homoscedasticity correctly
- Defined heteroscedasticity correctly
- Explained the difference in variance behaviour
- Identified why economists care about the distinction

If any item is incomplete, revise your explanation before continuing.

activities.reasoning_orientation: Focus on variance rather than regression coefficients. Examine what changes across observations and what remains constant. Build a mental model that separates constant error variation from changing error variation.
activities.self_explanation_prompt: In your own words, explain why two regression models with similar trend lines might differ in the variability of their errors.

materials.title: Error Terms and Residuals
materials.body:
## Error Terms and Residuals

A residual is the difference between an actual value and a predicted value.

Residuals help economists inspect whether error variation remains constant.

Large differences in variability across groups often suggest heteroscedasticity.

materials.title: Economic Variability Scenarios
materials.body:
## Scenario 1: Household Spending

Household Alpha earns £18,000. Spending patterns are similar to those of comparable households.

Household Beta earns £150,000. Spending patterns vary substantially.

## Scenario 2: Firm Profits

Firm Orion has annual profits near £50,000 with limited variation.

Firm Vega has profits near £5 million but outcomes vary greatly between years.

materials.title: Why Heteroscedasticity Matters
materials.body:
## Consequences for Inference

Heteroscedasticity does not necessarily bias coefficient estimates.

However, it can affect estimated standard errors.

As a result, confidence intervals, p-values and hypothesis tests may become unreliable.

materials.title: Analytical Walkthrough
materials.body:
1. Variance changes across observations.
2. Standard error estimates become less reliable.
3. Statistical tests rely on those estimates.
4. Conclusions about significance may therefore be misleading.

materials.title: Approaches to Addressing Heteroscedasticity
materials.body:
## Common Remedies

### Variable Transformations
Can stabilise variance.

### Robust Standard Errors
Adjust statistical inference without changing coefficient estimates.

### Weighted Least Squares
Useful when the variance structure is known.
